sourceChecks.scope: Read the full article via a browser User-Agent (usahockey.com returned HTTP 403 to a bare fetch, consistent with the standing lesson that hockeycanada.ca/usahockey.com may need a browser UA). It is a 2015 USA Hockey coach-development interview with Mike Guentzel (Univ. of Minnesota assoc. head coach). Directly supports exp26-u15-004's objective via the quote: 'a key is the faceoff -- having everybody on the same page, whether you have four on the kill or you have five on the power play. Win a puck, retrieve a puck, then get set up on the power play, or get a puck out on the penalty kill... You have a retrieval plan, you have to have a faceoff plan.' Supports exp26-u15-003's general coaching principle more loosely: PK teamwork and reacting to opponent pressure ('down a man, you really have to work together'; 'so many teams now are trying to dictate on the penalty kill... stepping up on the half-boards'), but the article does not specifically describe a slot-priority flank-shift tactic or any coordinates -- consistent with both scenarios' own source-use disclaimer ('original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified').
sourceChecks.ageFormat: General/coach-development article; its own editor's note states USA Hockey 'strongly recommends refraining from detailed and lengthy instructing on special teams tactics/systems until the 14U age classification at the earliest' -- notable supporting evidence that introducing PK/PP content at U15 (at/above 14U) is age-appropriate under this source's own guidance, and a caution against extending special-teams content down to younger bands (U13 and below) without separate justification.
sourceChecks.claim: General structured-plan and teamwork principles for penalty-kill and power-play play; does not certify the specific slot-lane-priority flank-shift system or the specific retrieval/backup/point role assignments as the one correct tactic.
